Every count below is measured against HEAD blobs via `git show`, not against the worktree.

### 🩺 Findings

<finding file="README.md" line="27" severity="high" confidence="measured">The REUSE-compliant badge is a static shields.io image asserting a compliance the tree does not hold and no instrument tests. Measured at HEAD over all 866 tracked files: 18 carry neither an SPDX tag nor a `.license` sidecar — `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`, `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `checker/hosted-plugin.json`, `dtd/forge-spec.json`, `dtd/licenses.json`, `dtd/sigils.json`, `monitors/manual.json`, `package.json`, both copies of `create-mcp-servers-dtd/templates/operations.json`, `artifacts/research/companion-9.0.0.json`, the five `docs/gifs/*.gif` and both `docs/tapes/*.jsonl`. There is no `REUSE.toml` and no `.reuse/dep5`, and `git ls-files` returns zero `.license` sidecars, so REUSE has no third route to cover them; `reuse lint` would report all 18 as files with missing licensing information and exit non-zero. No step of `.github/workflows/gate.yml` and no file under `checker/` names `reuse` at all. README.md:722 widens the same claim in prose — "AGPL-3.0-or-later OR EUPL-1.2, at your option, for every file in this repository" — while 18 files state no licence in any form REUSE reads. This is the one published claim in the tree with no instrument that can say no, in a repository whose thesis is that every claim carries one.</finding>

<finding file="checker/spdx-sweep.sh" line="16" severity="medium" confidence="measured">The sweep's skip list is `*.json|*.jsonl|*.gif|*.png|*.txt|*.log|LICENSE*|LICENSES/*|.gitignore|*.tgz`, whose extension set is exactly the set of the 18 uncovered files above, and the sweep's own negative control cannot reach it. The control at lines 26 to 38 plants `checker/zz-untagged-control.md` — a `.md`, which the skip list does not drop — and then asserts only that the enumerator listed it and that it lacks the tag; it never re-enters the main loop at lines 14 to 24 and never plants a `.json`. So the skip branch has no control at all, and the sweep prints `spdx-sweep: N files checked, 0 missing` over a hole it is structurally unable to see. Simulating the sweep's own skip list against HEAD in node gives checked=841, missing=0, while the census over all tracked files gives 18 uncovered: the difference is the untested branch.</finding>

<finding file="bin/rot-dtd-commander.mjs" line="390" severity="medium" confidence="measured">The install loop reads `if (!existsSync(src)) continue;`, so a `RUNTIME` entry whose file is absent is dropped in silence — no warning, no `failed++`, and the install still reports success. Nothing covers the forward direction. The coverage check at line 76 computes `missing` by comparing wanted names against `shipped`, which is itself built from `runtimeFiles(root)` at line 68, so it compares the list to itself and a dead entry passes. `checker/engines-sweep.mjs:59` checks only the reverse direction, that every engine a command invokes appears in `RUNTIME`. This phase is the one most exposed to it: 9.0.0 added nine entries, five of them documents under a directory that did not exist at v8.0.0, `dtd/sigil/`, and `LAW.SIGIL.3` requires those five at run time by name. Latent today — all 50 entries resolve on disk — but a rename in `dtd/sigil/` would ship an installation missing a file its own law demands, with a green install and a green gate.</finding>

<finding file="agents/dtd-contract-auditor.md" line="3" severity="medium" confidence="measured">The agent's `description` enumerates the shared subsets as four — "dtd/cc-core.dtd, cc-ask.dtd, cc-report.dtd, cc-record.dtd" — while `dtd/` holds 19 files matching `cc-*.dtd`, six of which this phase introduced or rewrote (`cc-cache`, `cc-sigil`, `cc-chain`, `cc-figure`, plus `typography.dtd` and `geometry.dtd` beside them). The body is correct and globs rather than enumerating, so the audit it performs is sound; the drift is in the routing surface. `checker/hosted-plugin.json:47` states the project's own position that "Selection is by description", which makes a description naming four of nineteen subsets the field most likely to misroute. `agents/` is byte-identical to v8.0.0, so this drifted passively as the subsets were added.</finding>

<finding file="LICENSES/MIT.txt" line="1" severity="low" confidence="measured">`LICENSES/` holds three licence texts, but a census of SPDX tags over all 866 tracked files returns exactly one expression, `AGPL-3.0-or-later OR EUPL-1.2`, 1600 times. No tracked file carries `SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT`. The upstream MIT grant is real and is stated in `LICENSE-MIT-taches-cc-resources` and in prose portions lines, but under REUSE a licence text in `LICENSES/` that no SPDX expression references is an unused licence and is reported as such. This is the same gap as the first finding seen from the other side: the licence file is correct, the machine-readable link to it is missing.</finding>

### 🩺 Verdict

The phase's own instruments are in good order, and the four folders this pass was sent to read are clean in every mechanical respect: no CR, no BOM, no stray control byte, a final LF on all twelve files, law numbering dense from 1 across all six subsets the range touches, and every law of `cc-cache`, `cc-sigil`, `cc-chain`, `cc-figure`, `typography` and `geometry` reached by something outside `dtd/`. `LAW.TYPO.8` looked orphaned to a text search of the sources, but `lib/typography.mjs` reports "36 TYPO.\* entities, 36 read, 0 orphaned" — the module spends it structurally rather than by citing its name, so the declaration is honoured. `bin/`'s two changes both hold: the new `C31` in `adiutor.mjs` exercises the cc-cache gate law in six live arms and the module runs 31 controls with 0 failing, and the nine `RUNTIME` additions in `rot-dtd-commander.mjs` all resolve, install through a recursive `mkdirSync`, and match `SIGIL.docs.count = 5` against the five real files in `dtd/sigil`. `monitors/manual.json` claims a 300 s ceiling and `monitors/commander-adiutor.mjs:61` sets exactly that. The gate chain reads 83 in `gate-sync`, `controls-sweep` finds 0 drifted across 33 claims, and `ai-slop` finds 0 slop in 290 swept sources.

What fails is narrower and older than the phase, and it is the class of defect this repository exists to refuse. A badge in the README asserts REUSE compliance; 18 tracked files carry no licence information in any form REUSE reads; there is no `REUSE.toml`, no `dep5` and no sidecar to supply it; and no workflow step or checker anywhere runs `reuse lint`. The one instrument that touches the question, `checker/spdx-sweep.sh`, skips precisely the extensions those 18 files use, and its negative control plants a `.md` and so can never exercise that branch. The tree therefore reports a clean SPDX sweep and displays a compliance badge over a hole neither can see. Every other claim in this release is measured in CI by something that has been tripped on purpose; this one is asserted by an image. That asymmetry is the finding, and it is why the verdict is not a pass.

### 🩺 Next

Decide first whether the 18 files should be covered or declared out of scope, because the two repairs differ. To cover them, add a `REUSE.toml` with one `[[annotations]]` block matching `**/*.json`, `**/*.jsonl` and `docs/gifs/*.gif` to `AGPL-3.0-or-later OR EUPL-1.2` — one file, no comment syntax needed, and it removes the reason the skip list exists. Then make the claim testable: add a gate step running `reuse lint`, or, if the dependency is unwanted, extend `checker/spdx-sweep.sh` to resolve `REUSE.toml` coverage for the skipped extensions and fail on an uncovered file. Either way, give that branch a control that can trip it — plant an untracked `checker/zz-untagged-control.json`, assert the sweep counts it as missing, then remove it and assert the count returns to zero, so the skip list is proven rather than trusted. Add `SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT` coverage for the upstream text, or drop `LICENSES/MIT.txt` if the prose grant in `LICENSE-MIT-taches-cc-resources` is the intended form. Separately, add a forward arm to `checker/engines-sweep.mjs` asserting every `RUNTIME` entry resolves on disk, which closes `bin/rot-dtd-commander.mjs:390` for the cost of three lines, and refresh the `description` of `agents/dtd-contract-auditor.md` to say "the shared subsets under dtd/" rather than naming four of nineteen. If the badge is kept before the lint exists, that is a decision to state, not a state to leave undisclosed.

COMPANION VERDICT: fail
